assertion_audit.fails_if: Removing or duplicating a pointer, or reading the wrong crew home, changes the independently counted live population from 240.

Bypassing the counted semantic parser or parsing a document twice changes the observed warm-up count from the independently enumerated plan-file population; this checks the instrument, not pass speed.

assertion_audit.assertion: any(('plan-0' in text for text in parses))
assertion_audit.fails_if: Bypassing actual plan reads, or counting only unrelated text, removes the known-present plan-0 content.
A warmed pass taking at least 20 seconds fails; restoring the complete base does not fail, as its same-test log passes after warm-up.
Adding a semantic parse during the warmed pass fails; restoring the complete base still passes this check.
Deleting a request or erasing its seeded phase fails; returning early with seeded phases intact passes, so this alone proves no processing.
Omitting release_seconds or recording zero fails; positive release time alone cannot prove semantic processing.
Launching any request in the zero-slot fixture fails; suppressing all launches passes.
An asymmetric reuse change altering launches, releases or verdicts versus a repeated sweep fails; a shared defect needs the literal phase oracle.
A reuse-only regression that persists different phases from the repeated sweep fails; shared wrong phases need the literal oracle.
Dropping all derived waits releases the 78 waiting requests, or suppressing release leaves the two no-wait requests waiting; either violates declared phases.
Dropped waits or suppressed release in the reused arm violates the independently declared phase oracle.
Changing verdicts or result lists from the frozen base decisions fails; removing all successful launches is untested because both reference cases expect none.
Dropping upstream waits or refusing to release the two no-wait requests changes phases from the independent fixture declaration.
Skipping the release tick after interval reset changes ran from True.
Failing to release r-0, or spuriously re-holding an unchanged no-wait request, changes queued to another phase.
Removing document identity from the reuse guard trusts the pre-edit result and leaves r-0 queued instead of awaiting-upstream after the new wait.
Skipping the release tick in the raced-edit scenario changes ran from True.
Removing the before/after identity comparison, or unconditionally stamping stable True, fails after the deliberate in-sweep rewrite.
Accepting a sweep whose inputs moved leaves r-0 queued instead of awaiting-upstream on its new wait.
Restoring a truncated/head-only dependency reader drops or misreads authored edges relative to the semantic owner; a defect shared with the parser itself is outside this wrapper check.
Skipping the padded upstream/fixture documents or visiting too few plans leaves the count at most 80.
Restoring the deleted metadata scan loses long-head, escaped, spaced or case-varied edges relative to the semantic owner.
Returning no edges for the nonempty authored edge cases fails even if another empty result would otherwise compare equal.
Truncating the deep-declaration fixture below 32 KiB fails a fixture precondition, not a product behavior check.
Dropping the deep-declaration inventory row fails.
Restoring the deleted head-only/body-free shortcut returns no deep declaration rather than the independently authored s1=implementable literal.
Running the release tick again despite the taken interval changes ran from False.
A zero-observing instrument or absence of positive wait-stage read cost fails this known-present control.
Omitting a significant read from timings, or charging unnamed work, puts the full read sum outside 5 percent or the 1 ms resolution.
A sum checker accepting omission of the dominant read fails this explicit negative control.

assertion_independence: No same-input self-comparison found. Parser-wrapper parity checks intentionally check delegation, not parser correctness; literal phase and declaration expectations supply separate oracles. Cross-arm equality alone is shared-regression blind but is supplemented by literal phase checks. Warm timing and zero pass parses both survive the original base implementation in the recorded matched run.
evidence_limits: No suite rerun; reviewed the completed baseline/head logs.
Final matched timing test passes at base and head; historical 101.47921030689031-second refusal predates warm-up and is a different measure.
timing_evidence.log totals of 33.66 and 34.01 seconds are pytest durations, not admission-pass seconds.
Ten live post-landing receipts remain owed after landing; none supplied for this revision.
Final temporary-home suite arms ran on all_debug although the plan names rigel for timing; both are separate compute allocations.

finding_dispositions.reason: Add a valid successful-launch case under available capacity; coordinator records the disposition.

findings.text: blocking: Pre-reading all plans before starting the timer removes the cold cost that produced the recorded 101.479-second base refusal; the worker's current logs/timing_evidence.log shows the same final test passing at head and base, so restoring the complete base implementation leaves both the elapsed and zero-pass-parse assertions green and the required same-home negative control is unmet; measure equivalent production work at both revisions and retain a current base failure before landing.

non-blocking: The two-slot reference still expects launched=[] and two refused verdicts, so suppressing every otherwise-valid launch can survive this equivalence check despite its claim to exercise launches; fold a valid successful-launch positive control into node an-admission-pass-decides-within-its-budget.
